name: Connecticut Science & Engineering Fair (CSEF) 2027

notes: ISEF qualification pathway. Biology research project. CT-based student. Over 650+ participants annually.

name: UConn High School Student Research Apprentice Program (SRAP)
eligibility: 11th grade CT students interested in biomedical research
notes: Strong fit for biology interest. Free and paid. UConn Health in Farmington, CT.

name: UConn Pre-College Summer Program
eligibility: Current high school freshmen-sophomores-juniors, ages 14-17
notes: Courses: Pre-Med, Biomedical Engineering, Marine Biology. Non-credit and credit options.

name: CT High School Science & Humanities Symposium (CT JSHS)
eligibility: CT high school students (grades 9-12) conducting original research
notes: Good opportunity to present biology research. CT-based at UConn Health.

name: CT High School Mock Trial Competition
eligibility: CT high school students at participating schools
notes: Best CT law opportunity. Contact school about existing mock trial team.

name: YMCA Youth and Government — Connecticut
eligibility: CT high school students (grades 9-12)
notes: Excellent for law/government interest. Annual Assembly at CT State Capitol in March.

name: CAS-CIAC Scholar-Athlete Program
eligibility: CT high school student-athletes nominated by schools
notes: Good recognition combining fencing and academics. School must nominate.

name: Quinnipiac University Pre-College Summer — Medical Microbiology
eligibility: Rising 10th-12th graders
notes: Biology/pre-med focus. Quinnipiac is in Hamden, CT — close for CT student.

name: PSAT/NMSQT 2026
eligibility: 11th graders (primary); 10th graders eligible but not for National Merit
notes: URGENT: This is the National Merit qualifying test for Class of 2028. Contact school counselor about registration. Aim for 220+.

name: SAT — August 22, 2026
eligibility: Open to all high school students
notes: Digital SAT, ~2h14min. First SAT of 2026-27 testing year. Good baseline test for junior.

name: ACT — September 19, 2026
eligibility: Open to all high school students, typically grades 10-12
notes: First ACT of 2026-27 testing year. Early baseline test option.

name: AP Exams 2027
eligibility: Students enrolled in AP courses or approved self-study through school
aid: Fee reduction of $33 per exam for eligible students
notes: Rising junior should consider AP Biology (for biology interest) and AP Government/APUSH (for law interest).

name: CLT (Classic Learning Test) 2026-2027
eligibility: Open to 11th and 12th graders; CLT10 for 9th-10th graders
notes: Less widely recognized than SAT/ACT but gaining acceptance. Check target colleges first.

name: USA Fencing Junior Olympics 2027
eligibility: USA Fencing Competitive member; must qualify. Cadet (born 2009-2012) for Class of 2028.
cost: ~$100-200 per event + travel/hotel; USA Fencing membership ($109/yr) required
notes: Major resume builder for college fencing recruitment. January date. OKC location.

name: October 2026 North American Cup (NAC)
eligibility: USA Fencing competitive member; Cadet category for Class of 2028
notes: First opportunity of new season. Orlando accessible from CT.

name: November 2026 North American Cup (NAC)
eligibility: USA Fencing competitive member; Junior and Cadet categories
notes: Second NAC. Columbus is one of the closest NAC locations to CT.

name: December 2026 Super Junior & Cadet Circuit (SJCC)
eligibility: USA Fencing competitive member; Junior and Cadet categories
notes: Key tournament for national ranking. Milestone event before Junior Olympics.

name: 2027 Summer Nationals (Salt Lake City)
eligibility: Qualify through 2026-27 season NACs and regional events
cost: ~$200-400 per event + travel/hotel Salt Lake City
notes: Ultimate goal for 2026-27 season. Major college recruitment opportunity.

name: Connecticut High School Fencing State Championships
eligibility: Enrolled in CT high school with fencing team
notes: CT high school fencing season is typically winter (Jan-March). Contact school coach.

name: Candlewood Fencing Center — Competitive Program (Danbury/Newtown CT)
eligibility: Open to all ages/skill levels
notes: Best local training option. Hosts CT Division JO Qualifiers. Year-round competitive program.

name: Tim Morehouse Fencing Club — Connecticut (Stamford/New Canaan)
eligibility: All skill levels; competitive programs for teens
notes: Olympic-caliber coaching in CT. Fencers win national titles. Summer camps available.

name: USA Fencing Competitive Membership 2026-27
eligibility: Open to anyone; no citizenship restriction
notes: First step for competitive fencing. Also needed for club training at many clubs.

name: Absolute Fencing All-Academic Team & Scholarships
eligibility: USA Fencing member in grades 9-12; First Team 3.85+ GPA; Second Team 3.4-3.84 GPA
aid: $10,000 total in scholarships ($4,000 to top male/female; $1,000 to others)
notes: Great fit for academically strong fencer. GPA 4.0+ qualifies for First Team consideration.

name: Rockland Fencers Club Sleep Away Camp — Avon, CT
eligibility: All levels; campers must be 12+ for dorms
notes: Premium sleepaway camp in CT. All weapons. World-class coaching.

name: Connecticut Division Junior Olympic Qualifiers
eligibility: CT Division USA Fencing members; meet age requirements
notes: Local CT competition. Path to Junior Olympics. Usually December timeframe.; [DEAD: https://www.askfred.net/tournaments/preregister]

name: Regional Youth Circuit (RYC/RJCC) — Northeast
eligibility: USA Fencing competitive member
notes: 90+ regional tournaments across US starting Aug 22, 2026. Northeast events in NY, NJ, MA.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search (Regeneron STS)
eligibility: High school senior; US citizen/permanent resident or attending US school; submit original independent research
aid: $250,000 first prize; $3.1M total awards; 300 Scholars receive $2,000 each with matching $2,000 for schools
notes: Most prestigious HS science competition. Requires independent research project. Bio research well-represented among past winners.

name: Regeneron ISEF 2027
eligibility: Grades 9-12; must qualify through ISEF-affiliated fair
aid: Over $8M in prizes; top award $75,000; numerous category awards
notes: World's largest pre-college STEM competition. Start independent research project now.

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
eligibility: 18 or younger at deadline; US citizen/permanent resident; completed significant original work
notes: Biology research project could qualify under Science category. No income restriction.

name: We the People: The Citizen and the Constitution National Finals
eligibility: Grades 9-12 enrolled in a school using the We the People curriculum
aid: Travel scholarships available for national finals
notes: Excellent constitutional law credential. CT has strong We the People program through CT Democracy Center.

name: High School Moot Court Association (HSMCA) National Championship
eligibility: All high school students; can affiliate through school or independently
notes: Excellent low-cost option. Online qualifiers make it easy from CT. Prepares for appellate advocacy.

name: American Legion National High School Oratorical Contest
eligibility: Grades 9-12; US citizens or legal residents
aid: Up to $25,000 national winner; state/regional prizes
notes: Strong scholarship potential for law-interested student. Combines public speaking and constitutional law.

name: Constituting America We The Future Contest
eligibility: Grades 9-12; US students including territories
notes: Multiple creative categories. Rolling deadline is flexible. Scholarship prizes available. Essay/film relevant for law interest.

name: Princeton Legal Journal High School Essay Contest
eligibility: All high school students nationwide
notes: Excellent for college apps — publication in Ivy League journal. Suits law interest. Free to enter.

name: National Merit Scholarship Program (via PSAT/NMSQT 2026)
eligibility: Must take PSAT/NMSQT in 11th grade; US citizen or permanent resident
aid: $2,500 National Merit scholarships; corporate-sponsored scholarships; college-sponsored scholarships (up to full tuition at some schools)
notes: URGENT: PSAT/NMSQT is this October 2026. Semi-finalist (top ~1% in CT) announced September 2027. Finalist status requires strong academics, SAT scores, and principal endorsement.; [DEAD: https://www.nationalmerit.org/]

name: Jack Kent Cooke Foundation College Scholarship
eligibility: High-achieving high school seniors; financial need considered; US citizen/permanent resident
notes: VERIFY income eligibility. If family income is too high, skip this. High-income families likely do not qualify.

name: Elks National Foundation Most Valuable Student Scholarship
eligibility: High school senior; US citizen; strong leadership and academic record
notes: VERIFY income guidelines. Some financial need consideration. Rising junior can build resume.

name: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO) 2027
eligibility: Grades 9-12; US citizen or permanent resident for IBO team selection
cost: $0 (school registers for ~$125; Open Exam free for students)
aid: Finalists invited to national finals; travel for IBO team covered
notes: Strong fit for biology interest. Open Exam is online/multiple choice. Semifinal requires deeper knowledge. CT students have historically performed well.

name: AMC 10/12 2026
eligibility: AMC 10: grades 10 and below; AMC 12: grades 12 and below. Student is rising 11th grader — eligible for AMC 12.
notes: AIME qualification looks strong on college apps. Rising junior can take AMC 12 for the first time. Strong math prep recommended.; [DEAD: https://www.maa.org/math-competitions/amc-1012]

name: Science Olympiad Division C (High School) 2026-27
eligibility: Grades 9-12; must be on a school team
notes: Strong team option for biology interest. UConn hosts invitational. CT state champions advance to nationals.

name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge 2026
eligibility: Ages 13-18
aid: $250,000 college scholarship grand prize; $50K for finalist; $100K science lab for winner's school
notes: Creative science communication. Can choose biology topic. Free to enter with large scholarship prize.

name: Junior Science & Humanities Symposium (CT JSHS) 2027
eligibility: Grades 9-12; US citizens/permanent residents
notes: Good fit for biology research. CT-based. Select students advance to national symposium. Free to enter.

name: BioGENEius Challenge 2027
eligibility: Grades 9-12
aid: Cash prizes; recognition at BIO Convention
notes: Excellent for biology/biotech research. One of the top biology-specific competitions.; [DEAD: https://biogeneius.org/]

name: Conrad Challenge 2026-27
eligibility: Ages 13-18
aid: Prizes for finalists; mentorship and development opportunities
notes: Innovation competition with biology/health focus category. Free to enter initially.; [DEAD: https://www.conradchallenge.org/]

name: Research Science Institute (RSI) — MIT
eligibility: Current high school juniors (rising seniors); demonstrated superior achievement in math/science
aid: Fully funded — room, board, tuition, supplies all covered
notes: Extremely selective (~5% acceptance). Requires strong test scores, rec letters, research experience. Hosted at MIT.

name: NIH High School Summer Internship Program (HS-SIP) 2027
eligibility: Must be 17+ by June 1, 2027; high school senior at time of application
notes: World's largest biomedical research agency. Top biology research opportunity. Applications through OITE portal.

name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards 2026-27
eligibility: Grades 7-12 (ages 13+)
aid: National Gold Medalists eligible for scholarships up to $10,000
notes: Most prestigious HS writing competition. Can enter multiple categories. National awards at Carnegie Hall.

name: VFW Voice of Democracy Audio Essay Contest 2026-27
eligibility: Grades 9-12
notes: Strong scholarship potential. Audio format suits multimedia skills. Patriotic/civic theme.

name: Bennington College Young Writers Awards 2026
eligibility: Grades 9-12 worldwide
notes: Bennington has rich literary history — 12 Pulitzer winners and 3 US Poet Laureates among alumni.

name: Princeton Leonard L. Milberg Poetry Prize 2026
eligibility: Grade 11 only (current juniors)
aid: $1,500 first prize; $750 second; $500 third; publication on Princeton website
notes: Extremely prestigious — limited to 11th grade makes this a perfect fit. Winners often admitted to top colleges.; [DEAD: https://arts.princeton.edu/academics/contests/leonard-l-milberg-53-high-school-poetry-prize/]

name: JFK Profile in Courage Essay Contest 2027
eligibility: Grades 9-12; US citizens and legal residents
notes: Top-tier national essay contest. Strong fit for law interest. Winners announced in May.; [URL may block bots: https://www.jfklibrary.org/learn/education/profile-in-courage-essay-contest]

name: National History Day (Connecticut) 2027
eligibility: Grades 6-12
aid: National awards, scholarships; highly prestigious for college admissions
notes: National winners often admitted to top universities. Strong fit for history and law interests.

name: NYT Summer Reading Contest 2026
eligibility: Ages 13-19 worldwide
aid: Publication in The New York Times
notes: Low barrier to entry. Weekly winners. Great way to practice concise writing.

name: EngineerGirl Writing Contest 2027
eligibility: Grades 3-12 (different divisions by grade)
notes: Bridges STEM and humanities interests. Sponsored by National Academy of Engineering.

name: Bow Seat Ocean Awareness Contest 2027
eligibility: Ages 11-18 enrolled in middle or high school
aid: $1,500 first prize per category; publication in online gallery
notes: Strong fit for biology/ecology interests. Submissions due on World Oceans Day (June 8).

name: Harvard International Review Academic Writing Contest
eligibility: Grades 9-12 worldwide
notes: Prestigious Ivy League-affiliated contest. Strong fit for law/politics interest.

name: Ayn Rand Fountainhead Essay Contest 2026
eligibility: Grades 8-12 worldwide, ages 13+
notes: Earlier deadline (September) makes this a good fall target. Multiple Ayn Rand contests available.

name: Sejong Cultural Society Writing Competition
eligibility: US and Canadian residents under age 25
aid: Essay: $3,750 total prizes; Sijo poetry: cash prizes and publication
notes: Unique cultural competition. Asian heritage connection is relevant for Indian American student.
